hyperliquid.def: The blockchain exchange where these markets trade. All data on this page comes from its public API.

hip3.def: Hyperliquid's system that lets outside teams (called deployers) list their own perpetual markets on Hyperliquid. Entropy is one such deployer.

entropy.def: A HIP-3 deployer on Hyperliquid (dex name io) that lists US stocks 24/7 and pre-IPO markets for Anthropic and OpenAI. This site is an unofficial community project, not run by Entropy.

perp.def: A futures-style contract with no expiry date. You bet on a price going up (long) or down (short) without owning the asset. Traders can use leverage, which makes prices move faster.

sparkline.def: The tiny line chart on each stock card. It shows the price over the last 7 days, with no axes, just the shape.

change_24h.def: How much the price moved compared with 24 hours ago, in percent.

change_7d.def: How much the price moved over the last 7 days, in percent. Matches the sparkline next to it.

preipo_perp.def: A perp on a company that is not listed on a stock exchange yet. Its price is set by traders, which gives a live read on what the market thinks the company is worth.

implied_valuation.def: The company value the perp price points to. On Entropy's pre-IPO perps, $1 of price = $1B of company value, so a price of 2,050 means $2.05T. It is a market signal, not an official valuation.

last_round.def: The company's most recent funding round with outside investors, and the valuation set in it (post-money, meaning including the new money). Source links are on each card.

multiple.def: Implied valuation divided by the last-round valuation. 2× means traders price the company at twice its last round. Below 1× means less.

premium.def: The same comparison as a percentage: multiple minus 1. A 2.1× multiple is a +110% premium to the last round.

lower_bound.def: The bottom of the price range Entropy's docs set for the market (the L value). The card shows what valuation it equals and how far the price is from it. See Entropy's docs for what happens at a bound.

upper_bound.def: The top of the price range Entropy's docs set for the market (the U value). The card shows what valuation it equals and how far the price is from it. See Entropy's docs for what happens at a bound.

no_ipo.def: The date in Entropy's docs by which the market is resolved if the company has not gone public. Shown with the days remaining.

mark.def: The reference price the exchange uses for a perp, for example to value open positions. It can differ a little from the last trade.

oracle.def: An outside reference price fed to the exchange. For US stocks it follows the public stock price while the market is open.

funding.def: A small payment between traders that keeps a perp's price close to the real price. When the rate is positive, longs pay shorts. When negative, shorts pay longs. It settles every hour.

funding_apr.def: The funding rate scaled to a yearly figure (hourly rate × 24 × 365, not compounded). Here it is averaged over the last 24 hours. +10% means longs pay shorts about 10% a year of their position size at that rate.

oi.def: The total dollar size of all positions that are still open. It shows how much money is riding on the market right now.

oi_cap.def: The maximum open interest Entropy allows on a market. When OI nears the cap, new positions can be limited.

volume_24h.def: The total dollar value traded in the last 24 hours.

session.def: The hours when the underlying stock market is open (US: 09:30 to 16:00 ET on trading days). A green dot means open. When closed, the Entropy perp keeps trading.

discovery.def: Entropy's stock perps trade all week, including nights and weekends, so the perp price shows where traders think the stock is heading while the stock exchange is shut.

luld.def: A cap on how far the mark price can move from the last regular-session close while the stock market is shut. It is set by the market's maximum leverage (1 divided by max leverage), so a 10× market can show at most ±10%.

weekend_gap.def: The price change between Friday's close and Monday's open, when US stocks cannot trade. We check whether the Entropy perp priced that gap correctly before the open.

predicted.def: The perp's move from Friday's close to just before Monday's open (09:15 to 09:30 ET). It is the weekend price discovery.

actual.def: The move from Friday's close to the first regular-session price on Monday (09:30 to 09:45 ET).

hit_rate.def: Share of weekends where the predicted and actual moves pointed the same way (both up or both down). Moves under 0.1% count as flat and are not scored.

abs_err.def: How far off the prediction was, ignoring direction: |predicted − actual| in percentage points. If predicted is +2.0% and actual is +3.5%, the error is 1.5 pp.

pp.def: The plain difference between two percentages. Going from 2% to 3.5% is 1.5 pp (not 75%).

captured.def: Predicted move divided by actual move, when both pointed the same way. 100% means the perp priced the whole move in advance. 50% means half.
